title: Code and derived data for "Brokerage without bridging: the middle class does not connect rich and poor in Brazilian cities"
description:
Code and city-level derived data for Samaniego, Menezes, Cantillán, Otero, Bucca & Evsukoff, Brokerage without bridging: the middle class does not connect rich and poor in Brazilian cities (submitted to Nature Cities).

The study tests whether any income stratum brokers contact between rich and poor residents, using directed mobile-phone contact networks built from 3.1 billion calls across nearly 300 Brazilian cities, with a Gould–Fernandez brokerage census evaluated against a mixing-preserving null model.

The repository is organised in two tiers. Tier 1 scripts reproduce every figure and table in the paper and its Supplementary Information from the derived data in data/derived/, which contain city- and stratum-level aggregates only. Tier 2 scripts build those derived data from per-city contact graphs; the graphs and the underlying call-detail records are confidential and are not included.

Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data under CC BY 4.0. A summary of the main result is at horaciosamaniego.github.io/middle-class-brokerage.
